pm_exper_user_4012_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I cope with feeling torn between my responsibilities and the people I care about?
pm_exper_user_4012_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When you feel torn between responsibilities and people you care about, you might try making the most of small moments of connection like calls or messages. Planning quality time in advance can help you honour both your work and your relationships without feeling pulled entirely in one direction.
(b) Because moving to a larger city has made you see your parents less and you miss them, you might ease the guilt by arranging regular video chats and sharing everyday moments. You could also bring them small gifts or treats from your city on visits, perhaps even a jar of sambal or other local flavours they enjoy, to keep that personal connection strong.
(c) If being far from your parents since relocating has left you feeling conflicted, try creating consistent moments of connection—like weekly calls or sharing photos. Scheduling occasional trips home ahead of time can help balance your commitments in the city with nurturing those family ties.
(d) Since you’ve felt guilty about not visiting your parents as often after moving to a bigger city, it can help to set up regular video calls and share little updates from your daily life. Planning visits in advance, even if they’re not frequent, can give you something to look forward to while still managing your local responsibilities.
